title: 8-year-old with progressive toe-walking and leg posturing, worse in the afternoon

provenance.citation: Synthetic case drafted 2026-10-17 for Rare Disease Detective; not derived from any individual patient.

chief_complaint: Parents: "She started walking on her toes and her right foot twists in. By the end of the school day she can barely walk, but she's fine in the morning."
history_of_present_illness: Normal development until age 6. Over 18 months, progressive toe-walking and inward turning of the right foot, later the left. Parents describe her as nearly normal on waking and on weekend mornings; by mid-afternoon she trips frequently and was moved out of PE. Recently stiff, slow handwriting late in the day. No seizures, no regression in learning, no episodes of sudden attacks. Pregnancy and birth uncomplicated, term, no NICU stay.

symptom_timeline.event: Intermittent right toe-walking noticed by teacher
Right foot inversion; orthopedic review, given ankle-foot orthoses
Left leg involved; falls in afternoons
Pediatric review queries spastic diplegia; referred to neurology

movement_findings.observation: Bilateral foot plantar flexion and inversion during walking, right worse than left, increasing over a 10-minute walk.
Mild dystonic posturing of the right hand during writing in afternoon clinic.
No involuntary movements at rest lying supine.

neurological_exam.tone: Mildly increased in the legs, variable, without a clear spastic catch
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ at knees and ankles bilaterally; plantar responses extensor-appearing bilaterally during gait, flexor when tested at rest lying down
neurological_exam.bradykinesia_screen: Mild slowing of toe tapping, no decrement

imaging.report: Normal. No periventricular leukomalacia. Normal spinal cord.

family_history: Mother (36) has had 'restless, stiff feet in the evenings' since adolescence, never evaluated. Father healthy. No consanguinity.
social_history: Lives with parents and younger sibling.
prior_workup_and_opinions: Orthopedics: no structural foot abnormality. Pediatrician: 'possible mild spastic diplegia' despite normal MRI and no perinatal history.
